clue.text: Odd shuffling very large old animals

indicators.note: shuffling the word Odd mixes its letters into a new order

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: Someone oddly shuffling some huge prehistoric creatures about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' looks like an adjective, but it is the fodder: its letters rearranged give DOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodos are flightless birds that died out in the seventeenth century, so they are long-gone creatures.

clue.text: Almost entirely foresee GB rower Redgrave's third son jumping from these?

indicators.note: almost entirely means all but the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: to divine is to foresee the future
an oar is a rower, one who pulls an oar in a crew

indicators.note: third picks out the third letter of the name Redgrave

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the Olympic rower Steve Redgrave and his family, with a nod to diving.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Redgrave is the famous British (GB) Olympic rower, which makes 'GB rower' read as one phrase; here GB stays as written and 'rower' alone is OAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers spring off these raised planks over a swimming pool, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Remove moggies, discharging a fire extinguisher — it's all kinds of sport!

parts.note: to remove cats would be to de-cat a place; moggies is British slang for cats

indicators.note: discharging lets the named letter out of the extinguisher word, so it is dropped

parts.note: halon is a gas used in fire extinguishers

explanation.surface: Clearing out the cats and setting off a fire extinguisher sounds like chaotic sport.
explanation.walkthrough: DECAT is a made-up verb: to remove the cats (moggies, British slang for cats). HALON is the extinguisher gas; 'discharging a' drops its A to leave HLON.
explanation.definitionFit: The decathlon is an athletics event made up of ten different track and field disciplines, hence a mix of sports.

clue.text: Swimming salmon mate — oddly, this is the result

definitions.text: Swimming salmon mate — oddly, this is the result

indicators.note: swimming says those picked letters move about into a new order
oddly keeps the first, third, fifth letters and so on of salmon mate

explanation.surface: Salmon pairing up, and the offspring that result from the mating.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of 'salmon mate' are SLOMT, which rearrange to the answer; the whole clue also describes a young salmon, the product of salmon mating.
explanation.definitionFit: A smolt is a young salmon at the stage when it first heads down to the sea, the offspring of spawning fish.

clue.text: One clicks what St Peter might have done

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hand-held percussion instrument that clicks

definitions.text: what St Peter might have done
definitions.meaning: second meaning: ..., as Peter the fisherman did on the Sea of Galilee

explanation.walkthrough: Read as three words, CAST A NET is what the fisherman apostle Peter did for a living; as one word it is the clicking instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Castanets are pairs of wooden shells clapped together in the hand, chiefly in Spanish dance, making a clicking sound.

clue.text: Lost cause in preparation? Not if you're hungry

definitions.text: Lost cause in preparation? Not if you're hungry

indicators.note: in preparation says the letters of lost cause are being made ready, worked into a new order as a cook works ingredients

explanation.surface: A doomed project still being prepared, which a hungry person would not give up on.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LOST CAUSE rearrange to the dish; the whole clue says a hungry person would never see this preparation as a lost cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassoulet is a hearty French stew of beans, sausage and duck, a dish prepared to feed the hungry.

clue.text: Fastens up slit

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: pins means fastens, as with a pin

explanation.surface: Someone does up a slit in a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fastens up' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'up' alone is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small cut, so both words name a narrow opening made with a blade.

clue.text: One plans development of the Arctic

indicators.note: development of means the letters of the Arctic are built into something new

explanation.surface: Someone drawing up plans for developing the polar region.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect designs buildings, drawing up the plans from which they are constructed.

clue.text: My boss accepts people to do what subeditors do

indicators.note: accepts means the first piece takes the second into its middle

parts.note: from a subeditor's view the boss is the editor, ED
men means people, as in staff or troops

explanation.surface: A subeditor's boss takes on staff to do the correcting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is spoken by the subeditor of the definition, whose boss is the editor, abbreviated ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct and improve a text, which is the work of a subeditor.

clue.text: I conquered, so cleric negotiated with us, leading to ever-worsening situations

parts.note: vici is Latin for I conquered, from Caesar's veni, vidi, vici

indicators.note: negotiated means the letters of so cleric and us are worked through into a new order

explanation.surface: A conqueror boasting of victory while a cleric negotiates terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar's boast veni, vidi, vici means I came, I saw, I conquered. SOCLERICUS rearranged gives OUSCIRCLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicious circle is a chain of causes where each problem makes the next one worse, looping back on itself.

clue.text: Showgirls (or Morris men?)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: female entertainers in a show
second meaning: read as ..., dancers covered in bells, as Morris dancers are

explanation.walkthrough: Morris dancing is an English folk dance whose dancers wear bells strapped to their legs, which makes them 'bell-y' dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: Belly dancing is a Middle Eastern performance dance, done professionally by female entertainers on stage.

clue.text: Nodding head at priestess before noon

indicators.note: before puts the pieces ahead of the letter for noon

parts.note: nut is slang for head
Io was a priestess of Hera in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Someone nodding off at a priestess just before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutation is a technical term for a nodding motion, of a plant or a spinning body's axis.

clue.text: Hey __ __ swindle!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the nursery rhyme begins Hey ... ..., the cat and the fiddle

explanation.walkthrough: The blanks take the same word twice, completing the nursery rhyme line.
explanation.definitionFit: To diddle someone is informal for cheating them out of money, a synonym of swindle.

clue.text: Dismisses Let It Be: Beatles' fifth and last hit

indicators.note: hit means the letters are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: the fifth letter of Beatles is L and its last letter is S

explanation.surface: A critic dismissing the Beatles' final hit album Let It Be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like a song hit, the Beatles' last single, but it is the signal to rearrange LETITBE plus L and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle something is to disparage it, treating it as unimportant, which is to dismiss it.

clue.text: Difficult request: a bit of buttered roll? A toastie's offered up

indicators.note: offered up says the hidden letters are read backwards
a bit of says the answer is a stretch of letters inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking for a piece of a buttered roll from someone's toastie seems a big ask.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'a bit' as part of the definition; 'a bit of' is the signal that the letters sit inside the words that follow, so the definition is just 'Difficult request'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for a demand that is unreasonably hard to meet.

clue.text: French food ordered in Sanssouci

indicators.note: ordered in suggests a takeaway, but means the letters of Sanssouci are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Getting French food delivered to Sanssouci, the Prussian king's palace in Potsdam.
explanation.walkthrough: Sanssouci is Frederick the Great's palace; its nine letters rearrange to the sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucisson is a French dry-cured sausage, a classic item of charcuterie.

clue.text: Praise the guts of fiery boxer, beating stout fellows

indicators.note: the guts of means the central letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Applauding a fiery boxer who has beaten a group of burly men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the guts of' seems to belong to the boxer alone, but it applies to all five words: fiery, boxer, beating, stout and fellows each give their middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to speak of something with high admiration, a formal synonym of praise used as a verb.

clue.text: Old long-distance communication could be a trumpet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the old British term for a long-distance phone call
second meaning: an elephant's trumpet is a call made through its trunk

explanation.walkthrough: A trunk call is the dated British phrase for a long-distance telephone call; the elephant's trumpeting is a call from its trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Before direct dialling, calls between distant towns went over trunk lines and were booked through an operator.

clue.text: Set aside a returned Bath bun Sally's not wanted

indicators.note: returned means what is left is read backwards
not wanted says the named word is removed from the bun's name

parts.note: a Sally Lunn is a large sweet bun associated with the city of Bath
taken as the name Sally

explanation.surface: Someone sends back a Bath bun that nobody wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sally Lunn is a rich bun from Bath, an English spa city; without Sally it is LUNN, which reversed after A gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a decision or marriage is to declare it void, setting it aside legally.

clue.text: Redcoat, before gaiety in Telford, spent money intended for someone else

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the shell of Telford
spent means Telford is emptied of its middle letters, leaving its ends
before puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: rust is a red coat that forms on iron
fun means gaiety

explanation.surface: A Butlin's holiday-camp entertainer (a redcoat) spending money on fun in the English town of Telford.
explanation.walkthrough: A redcoat is a Butlin's holiday-camp host, but here 'Redcoat' is the red coating that forms on iron, and Telford is an English town reduced to its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trust fund is capital held by trustees on behalf of a beneficiary, so it is set aside for another person.

clue.text: Sour fruit contributed by mother and child

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A mother and child sharing some tart fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small dark plum with a tart flavour, used mostly for jam and cooking.

clue.text: First chases second, being tearful

indicators.note: chases means the first piece runs ahead with the second following it

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
1ST, written with I for the digit 1, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: A race where the leader is chased by the runner-up, who ends up in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts First in front, but the one doing the chasing comes behind, so second leads in the answer; 1ST is written with an I in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist eyes are wet with tears, so moist describes someone close to crying.

clue.text: Wrong to take over from 20 with a Scotsman

indicators.note: take paired with from asks for the named letter to be removed from 20
from marks 20 as the word that the over abbreviation is removed from

parts.note: the answer to 20 Down
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
Ken, short for Kenneth, is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Wrong to let a Scotsman take over the previous clue's answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 Down is MOIST; taking over (O, cricket's abbreviation) out of it leaves MIST. Kenneth is a classic Scottish name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaken means in error, holding a belief that is not correct, which is to be wrong.

clue.text: I engaged in diplomacy without speaking

indicators.note: engaged in means the I is held inside the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact means diplomacy, sensitivity in dealing with others

explanation.surface: A diplomat says they worked silently in diplomatic talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood or implied without being stated out loud.

clue.text: Do you know what sushi rolls are wrapped in? Me neither!

definitions.text: what sushi rolls are wrapped in

parts.note: the reply's word neither stands for its partner conjunction, as in 'nor do I'
the speaker, me, is the first-person pronoun I

explanation.surface: One person asks what sushi is wrapped in, and the other admits ignorance.
explanation.walkthrough: The reply 'Me neither' is NOR I, which spells the seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nori is dried seaweed pressed into thin sheets, used in Japanese cookery to roll up sushi.

clue.text: In this you won't find solutions for 21 down and 13 across

definitions.text: In this you won't find solutions for 21 down and 13 across

parts.words: In this you won't find solutions for 21 down and 13 across
parts.note: a fruitless search: the clue sends the solver looking for entries whose directions are swapped, which do not exist

explanation.walkthrough: The grid has 21 Across and 13 Down but no 21 Down or 13 Across, so a hunt for them is futile.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild goose chase is a hopeless pursuit of something that cannot be found or caught.

clue.text: A string's bent by the ninth one?

indicators.note: bent means the letters of a string's are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A string on an instrument bent by the ninth one, perhaps a ninth string.
explanation.walkthrough: The ninth of the zodiac's twelve signs is Sagittarius; the question mark says the definition works by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A star sign is one of the twelve zodiac divisions, numbered from Aries, so there is a ninth one.

clue.text: Registers works

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a verb, works the soil

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like verbs, but the first is a noun, shop tills.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer tills a field by ploughing it, and shops ring up sales on tills.
